transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I'm here because my eating habits have gotten pretty restricted lately. I'm a firefighter, and originally, I just wanted to start eating cleaner to get in better shape for the lieutenant track. But it's kind of turned into me cutting my meals down to almost nothing. 

Lately, I'm basically just having black coffee, a protein shake, and a really small dinner. And I'm doing that even on shift days, when we're running calls and I know for a fact I've burned way more energy than what I'm taking in. It just feels like it went a bit too far, so I figured I should come in.
Have you been avoiding eating more because you're worried about gaining weight or becoming fat?

Yeah, I am. Honestly, if I step on the scale and it's up even just a pound—like, maybe after a big meal at the station or just from drinking extra water—I get this... this tight panic. It just feels like I’ve completely blown it. I worry that if I gain weight, people are going to see me as soft, or like I'm just out of control of myself. So, yeah, that fear is definitely a big part of why I avoid eating more.
Have you been doing anything else like exercising a lot, making yourself vomit, or using laxatives or diet pills to try to control your weight?

No, I haven't done any of that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or diet pills or anything like that. I do work out, but it's just my normal routine for the job—I wouldn't say I'm exercising excessively on top of what I already do at the station. It's really just the restricting what I eat.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or is your weight currently lower than what would be considered healthy for someone your height and build?

Yeah, I have lost quite a bit. I started noticing it when my gear and my station clothes started hanging a lot looser on me. We just had our annual fitness review, and they actually flagged my weight as being too low for my height and build. But honestly, even with them telling me that, part of me still feels like I need to keep trimming down just a little bit more.
Do you see yourself as overweight or notice specific parts of your body that you feel are too big, even if others might not see it that way?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I might not see my whole body as overweight, but... well, when I look in the mirror before work, I really zero in on specific parts. Mostly my waist and my face. 

I check to see if they look sharp enough, like there's no extra softness there. And if they don't look right to me, if I feel like they look too big... it really messes with my head. It just kind of ruins how confident I feel. I just don't feel as command-ready for the shift if I think I look soft in those areas.
How much does your perception of your body shape or weight influence your sense of self-worth or how you judge yourself?

It honestly influences it a lot. Like I mentioned, if I look in the mirror before a shift and my waist or face don't look sharp enough... it just completely throws me off. If I feel like I look soft or too big in those areas, I just don't feel confident. I feel like I'm not ready to lead or take command at work. My whole sense of how good I am at my job, or just how I feel about myself that day, really rides on how I think I look in the mirror.
Are you preoccupied with a perceived defect or flaw in your appearance, such as the shape of your waist or face, even if others don't notice it or reassure you that it's not a problem?

I wouldn't say I'm preoccupied with a defect or a flaw, really. It's not like I think my face or my waist are deformed or anything like that. It's just... I just want them to look lean. I don't think there's something wrong with how I was built, I just don't want any extra weight there. So, no, I don't think of it as a flaw.
Is your concern about your waist and face mainly about not wanting to gain weight or becoming fat, or is it more about how those areas look to you regardless of weight?

It's definitely about the weight. I mean, it's not just about how they look, it's about what that means. Like, if I step on the scale after a big meal at the station, or even if I just drank a lot of water, and I see it go up even a pound... I just get this tight panic in my chest. It feels like I've completely blown it. I just start thinking that everyone is going to see me as soft, or like I'm totally out of control. So yeah, it's really about not wanting to gain weight.

Is your main concern about restricting your food intake related to gaining weight, or is it more about achieving a specific look or level of muscle definition, even if that doesn’t necessarily involve gaining or losing fat?

It's definitely about the weight. I mean, I'm not... I'm not trying to look like a bodybuilder or get some crazy muscle definition just for the sake of it. It really all comes back to not wanting to put on fat. Like I said before, if I feel like I'm gaining weight, that's what freaks me out. So, yeah, keeping my food in check is really just to make sure I don't get heavier, it's not about trying to achieve a specific muscular look.
Have you found yourself thinking about food, weight, or body shape so much that it interferes with your ability to focus on other things, like work or relationships?

I'm still doing my job fine, but... I guess it has affected things a little bit at the station. I've started ducking out of the communal meals we have. When the crew orders food or cooks together, I usually just keep to myself and eat my own stuff. So, I'm definitely less part of the team than I used to be, just because I'm trying to avoid those situations. But as far as the actual work goes, I'm still focused.
Do you ever feel like you can't stop thinking about food or weight, even when you're trying to focus on something else?

No, I don't really have that happen. I mean... I definitely think about what I'm going to eat, or how to handle the meals at the station, like I mentioned. But it doesn't take over my mind when I'm trying to do other things. When we get a call, or if I'm just doing gear maintenance, my head is entirely on the job. It's not like a constant loop I can't turn off.
Have you ever had episodes where you feel like you're eating a large amount of food in a short period of time, and then afterward restrict your eating even more because of it?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I don't... I don't ever eat a large amount of food at once. I just stick to my routine and keep my portions small all the time. I don't really lose control like that where I'd need to restrict even more afterward, because I'm pretty much always keeping it in check to begin with.
Even though you know your weight is lower than what's considered healthy, do you still feel like you need to lose more weight or be even thinner to meet your personal goals?

Yeah, I do. I mean... my gear and my station clothes definitely hang a lot looser on me now. And during our last fitness review, they actually flagged my weight as being too low for my build, so I know what the numbers say. But even knowing that... yeah, honestly, part of me still feels like I should keep trimming down just a little bit more. I just feel like I haven't quite hit where I want to be yet.

Even though you're already underweight according to your build, do you still see yourself as needing to lose more weight, or do you believe that being even thinner would make you better in some way, like more in control or more fit for your job?

Yeah, I'd say it does. When I'm getting ready and looking in the mirror before work, I really focus on my waist and my face, just checking to see if they look sharp enough. If I feel like they don't... it honestly just messes with how confident I feel that day. It affects whether I feel, I guess, command-ready and sharp for the shift. So yeah, staying thinner definitely makes me feel more capable and in control on the job.
